guideTitle: 6 Best 500-lb Capacity Power Lift Recliners in 2026
metaDescription: Six power lift recliners listed for 500 lb or built for big and tall sitters, compared on seat width, motors, footrest length and extras before you buy.
introParagraphs: Shopping for a larger sitter is different from shopping for an average one. Seat width, frame construction and footrest length stop being nice extras and become the first things to check. A power lift recliner adds a motor that raises and tilts the chair forward, and for some people that makes standing from a seated position feel easier, though experiences differ.

The six chairs below are those whose listings point to big and tall users, and most state a 500 lb capacity on the product page. They split into dual motor and three-motor designs, with seat widths from 27.1 to 28 inches where a listing gives one. We evaluated them from specs and buyer feedback, not hands-on use.

None of these chairs is a medical device, and a lift chair does not treat a condition or prevent a fall. Confirm the listed capacity against your own weight plus clothing and anything in your lap, and consider asking an occupational therapist about fit and transfers.

products.name: REHOUSING Big Man Power Lift Recliner
products.description:
The REHOUSING is the widest seat in this group, at 28 inches, with a listed capacity of 500 lb and an extended footrest. Dual motors let the backrest and footrest move independently while the lift assist raises the chair. It adds an 8-point massage system with heat, and the maker splits the points between the backrest, seat and legs.

That width is its defining advantage and its main cost. A seat this broad gives larger frames real room, but the chair itself needs a generous footprint and a clear path through your doorway. The massage and heat are comfort extras and do not change the fit question.

Ownership means planning space first. Measure the room, the delivery route and the clearance behind the backrest for reclining. Against the Ymutrtcr at 27.1 inches, the REHOUSING gains about an inch of seat width, and next to the JUUXO it adds a heat and massage package the JUUXO listing does not stress.
products.bestFor: Larger sitters who want the roomiest seat in the group and independent back and footrest control.

products.name: Ymutrtcr 500 lb Power Lift Recliner
products.description:
The Ymutrtcr is pitched at people of 6 feet 5 inches and taller. It combines a 27.1 inch seat, a 26 inch tall back and a footrest the maker lists at 24.7 inches, which targets the problem of feet dangling past a short rest. Eight vibration nodes across the back, lumbar, thighs and calves come with five modes and lumbar heat.

The length is its real selling point. Many recliners run out of seat depth and footrest reach for tall users, and this one is built around that gap. If you are average in height, you will be paying for length you do not use, and the massage extras are comfort features rather than support.

Plan on space behind and in front when fully reclined, and measure the doorway before delivery. Compared with the REHOUSING at 28 inches, the seat is slightly narrower, but the footrest length is the stronger reason to choose it. The JIKFRIMA offers a detachable footrest if you want length you can remove.
products.bestFor: Taller users who struggle with short footrests on standard big and tall chairs.

products.name: DYNOX 9505L Big & Tall Power Lift Recliner
products.description:
The DYNOX 9505L uses a three-motor system that the listing says gives stable lift assistance and controlled reclining for larger users. Its 170 degree deep recline and extended footrest let you lean far back with fuller calf and foot support. The maker describes a reinforced frame built for big and tall users.

A third motor usually means a powered headrest or extra independent adjustment, which suits people who want to fine-tune posture for reading or television. The tradeoff is more mechanical parts and a heavier chair. The excerpt we reviewed does not state the capacity figure, so confirm it on the product page before buying.

In ownership terms, expect a substantial delivery and the need for rear clearance when the chair tips back toward 170 degrees. It sits above the dual-motor JUUXO for adjustability. Its sibling the DYNOX 9398L lists a 500 lb ceiling plainly, which makes that model the easier one to confirm.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want independent three-way adjustment and a very deep recline.

products.name: DYNOX 9398L Big & Tall Power Lift Recliner
products.description:
The DYNOX 9398L states the capacity up front, designed for big and tall users up to 500 lb, with an extra-wide seating area. A thickened reinforced steel frame is described alongside a stable tri-motor lift. The extended footrest adds room to stretch out, which the listing says helps taller users especially.

That clear capacity statement is its edge over listings that bury the number. The lay-flat recline suits napping and resting, though the seat width is not given in the excerpt we reviewed. Treat the frame language as the maker's description and check the warranty terms yourself.

Expect to plan for weight and clearance when moving the chair into the room, and to keep the cord path clear. Next to the DYNOX 9505L, it is the one that spells out 500 lb, while the 9505L emphasizes recline depth. The JIKFRIMA is the lighter-touch alternative if you value a removable footrest.

products.name: JIKFRIMA Big Man Power Lift Recliner
products.description:
The JIKFRIMA lists a tailor-made base frame supporting up to 500 lb and a lay-flat recline. Its extended footrest is detachable, so you can attach it for length or remove it to save floor space. Eight vibration points across the back, lumbar, thighs and calves come with lumbar heating.

The removable footrest is the useful twist. Taller users can keep it on, while someone in a smaller room may leave it off to reduce the reclined footprint. The listing does not give a seat width in the excerpt we reviewed, so compare dimensions on the product page.

Setup involves attaching the footrest correctly, so follow the maker's instructions and make sure it is secure before sitting. Compared with the Ymutrtcr and its fixed 24.7 inch footrest, the JIKFRIMA offers flexibility rather than a stated length. It pairs a similar 8-point massage with lumbar heat, much like the REHOUSING.

products.name: JUUXO Heavy Duty Power Lift Recliner
products.description:
The JUUXO is a heavy-duty recliner with a listed 500 lb capacity and an extended footrest. Dual motors give independent backrest and footrest control, so you can go from upright to a spacious lay-flat position. The lift function raises and tilts the chair forward to help with sitting and standing.

Its listing leans on the controls and the lay-flat position rather than on massage or heat. That makes it a plain, functional option for someone who does not want extra features. The tradeoff is that the excerpt gives no seat width, so confirm dimensions before ordering.

In use, expect to leave room behind the backrest for full recline and a short walk to the remote. Compared with the REHOUSING at 28 inches, you are trading a stated width for a simpler spec sheet. Versus the DYNOX 9505L with its three motors, the JUUXO keeps to two, which is easier to understand and maintain.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want independent controls and a heavy-duty rating without extra comfort add-ons.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A listed capacity is a limit for the whole load, so count your weight, clothing and anything in your lap. The JUUXO, JIKFRIMA, REHOUSING and Ymutrtcr list 500 lb, and the DYNOX 9398L says up to 500 lb. The DYNOX 9505L excerpt does not give a figure, so confirm it on the product page. Leave some margin instead of sitting right at the number.

Width decides whether the chair feels roomy or tight at the hips, and depth decides whether your thighs are supported. The REHOUSING offers 28 inches and the Ymutrtcr 27.1 inches, which are generous next to the 20 to 22 inches typical for average frames. Measure yourself seated and add a margin on each side. Check the interior seat dimension, not just the outside width.

A single motor moves back and footrest together, dual motors move them independently, and triple adds powered headrest control. The JUUXO and REHOUSING use dual motors, while the DYNOX 9505L and 9398L use three. More motors give finer positioning, but they add parts, weight and cost. Choose the number that matches how you actually sit, whether that is reading upright or napping flat.

A footrest that ends short leaves legs dangling, and tall users feel this first. The Ymutrtcr lists 24.7 inches and the JIKFRIMA offers a detachable extended rest, while the DYNOX 9505L reaches 170 degrees. Think about whether you want to sleep in the chair, since lay-flat and deep-recline designs differ. Always check the clearance needed behind and in front.

Heavier frames are more durable on paper but harder to move. The DYNOX 9398L describes a thickened reinforced steel frame, which adds weight. Measure your doorways, hallways and stairs before ordering, and decide who will help with setup. Follow the maker's assembly steps exactly and keep cables away from the lift path.

Heat and massage can feel pleasant, but they do not replace a correct fit. The Ymutrtcr, JIKFRIMA and REHOUSING each list 8 points of vibration massage with heat, while the JUUXO keeps its listing focused on controls. If you will not use them, skip the premium. Treat any massage claim as comfort, and an occupational therapist can advise on posture and transfers.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity and frame
howWeEvaluated.description: We read each listing for a stated capacity and compared how it was presented. Four picks name 500 lb directly and the DYNOX 9398L says up to 500 lb, while the 9505L excerpt gives no figure. We also noted frame descriptions such as the reinforced steel frame on the 9398L. A clearly stated number scored higher than vague language.

howWeEvaluated.title: Seat dimensions
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared the widths each listing gives and flagged where none appears. The REHOUSING leads at 28 inches, followed by the Ymutrtcr at 27.1. The JUUXO, JIKFRIMA and both DYNOX models give no width in the excerpts reviewed. Missing dimensions were treated as a gap to verify, not a flaw.

howWeEvaluated.title: Motor design and recline
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated dual-motor from three-motor chairs and weighed what each configuration adds. The DYNOX models offer three motors and the DYNOX 9505L reaches 170 degrees. The JUUXO and REHOUSING use two motors with independent back and footrest control. More adjustability earned credit only when the listing explained it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Footrest and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each chair accommodates leg length. The Ymutrtcr states a 24.7 inch footrest, the JIKFRIMA makes the footrest detachable, and the others describe an extended rest. Taller users were the reference case. Listings with a number outranked those with general wording.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each chair by its strongest trait. The REHOUSING leads on width, the Ymutrtcr on footrest length, the DYNOX 9505L on motors and recline depth, and the JIKFRIMA on a removable footrest. Heat and massage were treated as comfort additions. This is analysis based on product specs and buyer feedback.

howToChoose.intro: The motor count decides how finely you can adjust the chair.

cards.label: Dual motor
cards.text: Two motors move the backrest and footrest on their own, which covers most sitting and napping needs. The JUUXO and REHOUSING fall on this side. It is the simpler design, with fewer parts to maintain.

cards.label: Three motor
cards.text: A third motor typically adds independent control, such as a headrest, and often goes with deeper recline. The DYNOX 9505L and 9398L are the three-motor picks. Choose this if you read or watch television upright and want fine tuning; pick dual if you prefer simplicity.

faq.q: Does a 500 lb rating include clothing and items?
faq.a: You should treat it as the total load. Add your weight, your clothing and anything in your lap, such as a tablet or blanket. Leaving some margin is sensible, and the maker's published figure for your exact model is the one that counts.

faq.q: Is a three-motor chair better than a dual-motor one?
faq.a: Not automatically. A third motor adds adjustability, as on the DYNOX 9505L and 9398L, but also more parts and weight. A dual-motor chair like the JUUXO or REHOUSING handles back and footrest independently. Pick based on how finely you want to adjust.

faq.q: Will a lift recliner prevent falls?
faq.a: No chair can promise that. A lift function is designed to raise and tilt you forward to make standing feel easier, and experiences vary. An occupational therapist can advise on transfers and positioning for your situation.

faq.q: Are heat and massage worth paying for?
faq.a: They are comfort extras, and they do not change how well the chair fits. The Ymutrtcr, JIKFRIMA and REHOUSING each list 8-point massage with heat. If you would use them, they are pleasant; if not, a simpler chair like the JUUXO can be a better use of budget.

faq.q: How much space does a big recliner need?
faq.a: Allow clearance behind the backrest and in front of the footrest when fully reclined. The DYNOX 9505L at 170 degrees leans back further than many. Measure the room and the delivery route, including doorways and turns, before ordering.

faq.q: What should I check when a listing leaves out the seat width?
faq.a: Look at the dimension sheet on the product page, or ask the seller. Several chairs here, including the JUUXO and JIKFRIMA, give no width in their listing text. Compare the interior seat measure against your own hip width plus a margin.

Many are shipped heavy and need two people. Follow the maker's steps exactly, especially for parts like the JIKFRIMA's detachable footrest. Check that cables are clear of the lift path, and ask someone to help move the frame.
